title: Path Traversal via Pathname#join
security_mechanism: Pathname#join replaces the whole path when the argument is absolute — Pathname.new('/safe/dir').join('/etc/passwd') is /etc/passwd — and '..' segments survive in plain File.join/File.read construction, so a single join call never confines the result to the base directory. Dir.glob expands metacharacters (*, ?, [, {) appearing in an attacker-supplied pattern beyond the intended directory, and archive entry names containing absolute paths or '..' escape the extraction root when unpacked verbatim. Temporary names built as Dir.tmpdir plus a fixed string are predictable, letting a local attacker pre-create a symlink at that path.

source_sink_clues.source: Request-supplied file names, download paths, glob patterns, archive entry names, and any path component from external input.
source_sink_clues.sink: Pathname#join / File.join / File.read with attacker components; Dir.glob with input-derived patterns; archive extraction loops; hard-coded temporary file names

tracking_guards: Require File.basename extraction plus a realpath containment check (candidate.realpath starts_with? base.realpath) before use; require glob patterns to be constant with input escaped (Dir.glob escape) or results filtered; require archive entry names validated against the extraction root; require Tempfile.create for temporary files.
not_candidate_when: The component is basename()'d and containment is verified via realpath before any read/write, the glob pattern is constant with input escaped or result-filtered, archive members are validated against the target root, or temporary files come from Tempfile.create.
public_references: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html
